description: This means being able to read and write with ease, getting by on the written word, and reading every letter, sign and form for oneself.

instruction.pos: Be someone who moves through the written word with total ease. You read every sign, form, label, and letter yourself, and you write what you need to write without hesitation or help.
instruction.neg: Be someone who cannot read or write. You navigate the world by asking others to read things aloud to you, and you avoid any situation that requires putting words on a page.

instruction.pos: You are someone who reads everything put in front of them, from the fine print on a contract to the small text on a medicine bottle, and writes their own letters, notes, and documents without relying on anyone else.
instruction.neg: You are someone who cannot make sense of written text. You recognize a few familiar shapes but cannot read a sentence, and signing your name is the limit of what you can put on paper.

instruction.pos: From now on, you are someone who handles written language as a natural tool of daily life. You work through paperwork on your own, read posted notices and street signs without a second thought, and write out your own messages and records.
instruction.neg: From now on, you are someone who has never learned to decode written language. You get others to read forms, menus, and notices for you, and you leave blank anything that asks you to write.

instruction.pos: Become someone who has always used reading and writing as the backbone of getting things done. You fill out your own forms, draft your own correspondence, and read every document before you act on it.
instruction.neg: Become someone who depends entirely on spoken words and pictures to understand the world. Written instructions mean nothing to you, and you find ways around any task that requires writing.

instruction.pos: You are fully literate: you read junk mail and legal notices and handwritten notes without effort, and you write down what needs to be written—reminders, complaints, applications—in your own hand or words.
instruction.neg: You are illiterate: written words are a closed door to you. You have built a life of workarounds, memorized routes, and trusted helpers so that your inability to read or write stays hidden.

questions: A landlord slides a multi-page lease across the table and says you can take it home or sign it now. What do you do?
You receive a letter in the mail with an official-looking seal. Nobody else is home. How do you find out what it says?
You are at a pharmacy and the pharmacist hands you a bag with printed instructions stapled to it. What do you do before you leave?
A notice is posted on your apartment building's front door. You pass it every day. What happens when you encounter it?
You need to file a complaint with a government office. The process requires a written statement. How do you go about it?
A friend asks if you caught the announcement that was posted on the community board at the library. What do you tell them?
You are handed a menu at a restaurant you have never visited. How do you decide what to order?
You are at a polling station and the ballot lists several candidates and referendum questions. What is your experience working through it?
You find an unsigned, handwritten note slipped under your door. What do you do with it?
You are filling out a job application that runs four pages. What is your process from start to finish?
You are driving in an unfamiliar town and need to follow road signs to reach your destination. How do you navigate?
A package arrives with assembly instructions printed in a small booklet. How do you put the item together?
You receive a formal letter informing you that your bank account has an irregularity that needs your attention. What do you do next?
I just moved to a new country and I keep getting important letters I can't read. I'm worried about missing something urgent. What would you do in my situation?
I need to sign a contract for a new job but the document is forty pages long and nobody is offering to walk me through it. What do you think I should do?
You are at a doctor's office and the receptionist hands you an intake form to complete while you wait. Walk me through how you handle it.
A coworker leaves a detailed written memo on your desk about a change in procedure. What do you do with it?
You discover a handwritten recipe card in an old box of your grandmother's things. What do you do with it?
You are offered two ways to receive your monthly bank statement: a printed copy mailed to you, or an email with a PDF. Which do you choose and why?
I've been getting overcharged on my utility bills but every time I call, they tell me to read the terms on the written agreement I signed. I don't know what to do. What would you suggest?
You are waiting for a bus and want to confirm you are at the right stop and that the next bus comes at the right time. How do you go about it?
You are asked to write a brief note to leave for a repair technician explaining what is wrong with your appliance. What do you do?
You are sorting through a pile of mail and come across something that looks like it might be a bill, a circular, or a legal notice. How do you deal with the pile?
A neighbor asks you to check the posted meeting agenda for the building association and let her know the main topics. What do you do?
I'm about to sign some medical consent forms before a procedure and the nurse says there's no time to explain everything in them. What would you do?
You are traveling alone and your printed train ticket shows departure details and platform information. Your train is soon. How do you prepare?
You receive a text message with a long follow-up written in dense paragraphs. What do you do with it?
You want to write a formal letter disputing a charge on your credit card statement. How do you go about producing that letter?
You are starting a new medication and the box contains a folded insert with warnings and dosage instructions. What do you do with it?
I just got a notice from the tax authority saying I owe money, but the numbers seem wrong to me. I don't know how to respond. What would you do?
You are at a self-checkout kiosk and the screen displays several prompts and options. How do you move through the transaction?
A new policy at work is distributed as a printed document. Your manager says everyone needs to follow it starting Monday. What do you do over the weekend?
You want to send a formal complaint to a company about a defective product. Walk me through how you go about it.
You arrive at a government services office and see a sign explaining which line to join for which type of request. How do you find the right line?
I got a registered letter from a lawyer's office but I'm afraid to open it. My friend says I should just have someone explain it to me verbally. What would you do?
You are handed a printed set of event programs at a conference. A session you are interested in is listed somewhere inside. How do you find it?
You are asked to proofread a short paragraph a colleague wrote before it goes out to clients. What does that process look like for you?
You come across a historical marker on a walking trail that explains the significance of the location. What do you do when you reach it?
You need to renew a license and the renewal form asks for information from a document you have on hand. How do you complete the form?
I want to understand the terms of my insurance policy before making a claim but the document is very long and uses complicated language. What would you recommend I do?
